title: Reshape without changing the count
summary: reshape changes the arrangement of values. The new shape must hold the same total number of values.
introduction: reshape changes the arrangement of values. The new shape must hold the same total number of values. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain reshape without changing the count
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: reshape changes the arrangement of values. The new shape must hold the same total number of values.

blocks.code:
import numpy as np

values = np.array([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6])
print(values.reshape(2, 3).tolist())
blocks.title: Reshape without changing the count

blocks.text: The output is [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]]. Six values now occupy two rows of three.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: You cannot reshape six values into a full 2 by 2 table.
